digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI/CD — Gerrit Verified workflow
propositions: Gerrit Verified dispatch workflow saturates the GitHub Free plan 20-concurrent-job limit during bursts of independent patchsets, causing runner job queue depths of 22+ and wait latencies of 800+ seconds, not tickets-branch pushes as previously attributed.

The current Verified workflow executes 17–24 runner-backed jobs per dispatch (13 full-route fan-out with 0–7 mutation shards) immediately after classification, creating peak simultaneous demand of 19 jobs and macOS-specific contention within the shared 5-macOS ceiling.

Option A bundles four short Ubuntu preflights into one sequential job and caps mutation parallelism to 3, reducing full-route demand from 17 to 14 jobs and peak simultaneous from 19 to 12, with negligible latency impact and no coverage loss.

Option C moves macOS/Python 3.13 from pre-merge Verified to six-hourly main branch health, saving 9–11 minutes per run but accepting 6-hour macOS regression detection latency as a pre-merge coverage policy change.
Option D upgrades the organization from Free to Team plan (20→60 concurrent jobs) with recurring billing impact and no change to the 5-macOS bottleneck.
The investigator has completed read-only evidence collection and decision-brief analysis without implementing remediation; operator approval is required before implementation of any chosen option.
